thread:
emma: Alerts from ENG SSO that some enterprise customers lose admin roles intermittently after OIDC client rotation this morning. Login OK, elevated calls 403. Anyone seen this pattern? :rotating_light:

ryan: saw a blip in claim-enricher around the same time. It authenticated tokens but enrichment failed with invalid_client.

devops-bot: rotation-job rotate-oidc-client service=enterprise-portal region=us-west triggered=1749954280 status=SUCCESS actor=automation-svc

emma: claim-enricher log (redacted):
```
INFO validate token_id=t-11
ERROR enrich_claims token_id=t-11 error=\"introspect 401: invalid_client\" rq=rq-12
WARN fallback_roles token_id=t-11 roles=[user]
```

ryan: that looks like introspection creds couldn't be used. Where is the introspect secret stored?

key-ops: secrets-manager keyarn=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123:key/rotated-key shows Decrypt AccessDenied at 1749954285..1749954300. New key policy missing service role.

emma: so automation swapped alias -> secret updated -> services can't decrypt -> claim enrichment returns 401 -> RBAC falls back. Automation reported success because it didn't validate decryption.

ryan: immediate actions: (1) patch key policy to include service role (2) restart claim-enricher pods after policy change (3) update rotation job to validate decrypt as the service principal before marking success.

key-ops: policy updated, restarted pods, canary decrypt succeeded. Roles restored.

emma: follow-ups: add key_id + secret_version to secrets fetch audit logs (for compliance trace), change claim-enricher to retry on 401 for N seconds before removing admin roles, and update runbook for safe alias rotation (overlap + precheck). Ticket: ENGSEC-7810.

audit-bot: audit:secrets fetch_attempts=9 tenant=enterprise-acme first_seen=1749954279 last_seen=1749954310 key_ids=[key/old-id,key/new-id]
